context.clinical_context_summary: 80-year-old Male with extensive cardiovascular history including CABG, NSTEMI, rheumatic and nonrheumatic aortic stenosis, acute diastolic heart failure, hypertension, and hyperlipidemia. Also has history of sepsis, acute kidney failure, and UTI. Currently on aspirin 81mg for antiplatelet therapy and various supplements. Presents with FEVER (mean temp 38.09°C, max 39.1°C). Given his cardiac history and prior sepsis, this patient is at HIGH RISK for hemodynamic instability and recurrent sepsis. Temperature readings appear consistent with standard oral/temporal measurement given the elevated mean during febrile illness.
context.rationale: Thresholds are personalized for this 80-year-old with severe cardiovascular disease (CABG, aortic stenosis, heart failure, prior NSTEMI). His baseline BP appears chronically low (mean SBP 87, DBP 52), likely reflecting cardiac dysfunction; however, maintaining warning threshold at SBP ≥90 is critical to ensure adequate perfusion. Heart rate upper limit set conservatively at 90 (normal) and 100 (warning) given his cardiac history where tachycardia increases myocardial oxygen demand. SpO2 threshold set at 94% normal given his age and cardiac status. Respiratory rate thresholds account for his heart failure where rates >24 suggest decompensation. Temperature thresholds are standard as current readings suggest true fever requiring monitoring for sepsis recurrence.
